author: GamingBolt
description:
Crimson Desert has already changed so much over the course of the year, but that doesn’t mean its modding community has been happy to let the developer cook on its own. From changes to the traversal mechanics to difficulty sliders that can make the combat system feel like its raw power is matched by your foe’s ferocity, there are so many cool ways to make Pywel feel different from what you’re used to, and perhaps growing a little bored of.

We’ve put together a few ones that you can mix and match to see just how much of a change they can bring to the experience. Of course, we’ve been happy to tell you why they’ve made the cut too!

author: GamingBolt
description:
Before it started piling on the numbers and spin-offs, before it ventured into the third-person or even fully 3D space, before it commanded a gargantuan budget – heck, when it was still DMA Design instead of Rockstar North, Grand Theft Auto launched in 1997 for, surprisingly, MS-DOS and Windows (it arrived on PlayStation One about a month later).

Originally called Race 'n' Chase, it was, by all accounts, hated by leadership. You see, DMA Design wasn't a company that specialized in crime epics or game mechanics revolving around cops and robbers
title: GTA 1: Nearly 30 Years Later, Is It Worth Playing Before GTA 6?

author: GamingBolt
description:
As many complaints as I have about Castlevania: Belmont's Curse, its various elements can come together fairly well. It's just that several of them don't feel consistently great, oscillating between fun and frustrating, seemingly on a whim (not that there's an excuse for the backtracking). The art direction and music are consistently great, even if some tracks feel more fitting of The Rogue Prince of Persia than Castlevania. There are also some baffling performance drops when scanning through the map. At the very least, whether swinging from pillar to post or engaging a gigantic boss and narrowly avoiding its attacks, the frame rate is fairly solid.

Even with all these complaints, Belmont's Curse still makes a strong case for a solid foundation on which future titles can thrive. But after years of waiting for a new Castlevania, especially one that returns to the series' 2D roots, I was hoping for something more than just good, especially given the sheer quality of games nowadays.
title: Castlevania: Belmont's Curse Review - A Great Game With Flaws
